Efforts to apply transformer-based language models (TLMs) to the problem of reasoning in natural language have enjoyed ever-increasing success in recent years.
The most fundamental task in this area to which nearly all others can be reduced is that of determining satisfiability.
The problem instances of satisfiability in natural language can belong to different computational complexity classes depending on the language fragment in which they are expressed.
Hence, we investigate how problem instances from varying computational complexity classes and having different grammatical constructs impact TLMs’ ability to learn rules of inference.
